summary: Core reactive MVVM primitives, commands, activation, routing, platform-neutral guidance, and upgrade paths for legacy ReactiveUI applications.
recommendedPatterns: Use ReactiveObject and ReactiveCommand for mutable state and user actions.
Prefer WhenAnyValue and OAPH/source-generator derived properties over imperative setter side effects.
Plan upgrades from legacy ReactiveUI codebases by modernizing startup, disposal, command handling, and generator usage incrementally.
avoidPatterns: Do not create long-lived subscriptions in constructors without disposal.
Do not mutate UI-bound state from background threads.
Do not leave legacy initialization, obsolete collection types, or stale package combinations in upgraded apps when a modern equivalent exists.
setupSteps: Select the correct platform package for the target UI stack.
For legacy upgrades, align packages first, then replace obsolete patterns incrementally with modern ReactiveUI guidance.
commonPitfalls: Mixing imperative state mutation with derived observable state.
Failing to scope bindings with activation on XAML-style platforms during upgrades.

options: WPF, WinForms, WinUI, MAUI, Blazor, AndroidX, Avalonia, or Uno host package
Core routing or DynamicData-based ReactiveUI.Routing extensions
App-wide main-thread/task-pool sequencers and service registrations
packageSelection: Default: ReactiveUI plus the matching lean platform package and a direct ReactiveUI.Primitives reference when its analyzers/APIs are used.
Full System.Reactive compatibility: ReactiveUI.Reactive plus matching *.Reactive platform packages.
Add ReactiveUI.Routing or ReactiveUI.Routing.Reactive only for DynamicData change-set routing/auto-persist helpers.
Add ReactiveUI.Testing only to test projects.
sourceGeneratorGuidance: Use ReactiveUI.SourceGenerators first for properties, OAPHs, commands, IViewFor, IReactiveObject, collections, and supported hosts.
Use ReactiveUI.Binding's included generator first for static observation and binding call sites.
Use manual core APIs only for dynamic or unsupported generator scenarios and document the limitation.
compatibilityNotes: ReactiveUI 24 lean and .Reactive distributions share the same Primitives engine and MVVM shape but expose different reactive interop types.
Lean uses RxVoid/ISequencer/Signal; .Reactive uses Unit/IScheduler/Subject for existing Rx boundaries.
Core routing remains in ReactiveUI; DynamicData-based routing extensions moved to ReactiveUI.Routing.
migrationGuidance: Move Fody and handwritten boilerplate to ReactiveUI.SourceGenerators before broad behavioral refactoring.
Prefer lean ReactiveUI/ReactiveUI.Primitives for new code; use the .Reactive family only when existing public API compatibility requires it.
Move constructor-created view subscriptions into WhenActivated and preserve command exception/scheduler behavior with tests.
